data.title: Denmark joins race for Indian tech talent, eyes deeper technology ties
data.description:
Denmark's Minister for Foreign Affairs, Lars Løkke Rasmussen, visited Bengaluru on November 27, 2026, to witness India's impressive tech capabilities and discuss the deepening of technology cooperation between Denmark and India, according to the Embassy of Denmark.
 
While exploring the frontiers of space, quantum technology, and defence in India's premier tech hub, the minister also highlighted the potential for Denmark to attract Indian tech talent, the embassy said.
 
“You have an enormous talent pool with exactly the skills that Danish companies are looking for,” Løkke Rasmussen said.
 
During the visit, the minister launched the report 'Access to Tech Talent in India' by Innovation Centre Denmark in Bengaluru. The report examines the potential for Denmark to attract talent from India. The aim is to meet the domestic challenge of an expanding tech sector with an inadequate supply of skilled labour. The minister acknowledged that Denmark faces competition for those workers.
 
 
“We are not the only ones trying to attract Indian talent,” he said. “So, we also want to make Denmark an attractive place for skilled Indian professionals to go for work.”
 
Denmark has an Innovation Centre at the Consulate General in Bengaluru. The embassy describes the consulate as the only permanent Danish diplomatic representation in India outside New Delhi.
 
“Denmark and Karnataka both understand that innovation is key to our prosperity,” Løkke Rasmussen said. “Our economies thrive on technological advances, and we have much to offer each other. That is why we have partnered with Karnataka and established an Innovation Centre at our consulate here in Bengaluru.”
 
Space, quantum and defence
 
The minister visited C-CAMP, where Denmark's Novo Nordisk Foundation and BioInnovation Institute are present. He also visited quantum company QpiAI. Both visits were to discuss innovation and quantum technology.
 
At the Indian Space Research Organisation (Isro), the minister discussed possible cooperation in space. The talks included how Danish small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and startups can collaborate with Isro.
 
The minister also visited Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL). Components from the Danish company HBK are being used in the Advanced Light Helicopter and Light Combat Helicopter. They are also used in research and development (R&D) testing of the Tejas fighter jet.
 
He also met Karnataka IT Minister Priyank Kharge and Danish companies present in Karnataka. They discussed the role of global capability centres (GCCs) and India's large tech talent pool.
 
The embassy lists several recent Danish investments in the state.
 
For instance, PowerCurve, a Danish wind turbine blade optimisation company, established its Indian subsidiary in Bengaluru in October 2026.
 
Norican Group expanded its manufacturing operations in Tumakuru with a new greenfield facility in June 2026. The facility produces DISA machines, mould handling systems, and SIMPSON products, strengthening its Indian manufacturing capabilities, according to the embassy.
 
KK Wind Solutions inaugurated its largest manufacturing facility in Asia at Dobbaspet, near Bengaluru, in May 2025. The 17,000 square metre facility produces power converters and control systems for wind turbines, with capacity for up to 400 employees.
 
The visit to Bengaluru will be followed by a visit to New Delhi on Saturday, according to the embassy.

data.title: RBI allows white-label ATM operators to buy cash directly from its offices
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Friday allowed white-label ATM operators to purchase cash directly from its issue offices in wholesale lots, besides sourcing it from banks other than their sponsor banks, in a move that could ease cash replenishment for these operators.
 
In its circular, the RBI said that operators can purchase cash in quantities exceeding one lakh pieces, and in multiples thereof, of any denomination, against full payment. They can also source cash from scheduled commercial banks, cooperative banks, and regional rural banks.
 
The directions, effective immediately, consolidate the existing regulatory framework for white-label ATMs. Operators are required to maintain a minimum net worth of ₹100 crore and ensure ATM deployment is skewed towards semi-urban and rural areas. The minimum deployment ratio across metro, urban, semi-urban, and rural centres is 1:2:3.
 
 
The RBI has also allowed white-label ATM operators (WLAOs) to have multiple sponsor banks and offer interoperable cardless cash withdrawals (ICCW) using the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) for customer authorisation. Settlement of such transactions will be through the National Financial Switch or ATM networks.
 
Withdrawal limits for ICCW transactions will be aligned with those for regular ATM withdrawals. Operators will not be permitted to levy charges beyond the prescribed interchange fee and customer charges.
 
WLAOs can also offer bill payment and interoperable cash deposit services, subject to technical feasibility and certification by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
 
In a separate circular on cash withdrawals, the RBI retained five free monthly transactions at a bank's own ATMs, including financial and non-financial transactions. At other banks' ATMs, customers will be entitled to three free transactions in metro centres and five in non-metro centres, subject to an overall cap of five if transactions are undertaken across both categories.
 
The maximum cash withdrawal at other banks' ATMs will be ₹10,000 per transaction. Charges beyond the prescribed free transactions will be capped at ₹23 per transaction, plus applicable taxes.
 
Transactions failing due to technical reasons or non-availability of cash will not be counted towards the free transaction limit or attract charges.
 
Cash withdrawals at point-of-sale (PoS) terminals will be permitted through debit cards, full-KYC prepaid payment instruments, and UPI, with a limit of ₹2,000 per transaction and ₹10,000 a month. Charges, if levied, cannot exceed 1 per cent of the transaction amount. The facility will be available even without a purchase.

data.title: Mini targets over 70% sales growth in India in 2026, eyes 15-20% EV share
data.description:
BMW Group’s British luxury car brand Mini expects its India sales to grow by over 70 per cent in calendar year 2026, driven by the localisation of its petrol-powered Countryman C, network expansion, and new product launches. The company expects electric vehicles (EVs) to initially account for 15-20 per cent of its India sales.
 
Mini on Friday launched its new-generation all-electric Cooper SE at ₹53.9 lakh, along with three special editions developed in collaboration with British fashion designer Sir Paul Smith, priced between ₹55.75 lakh and ₹61.5 lakh (ex-showroom).
 
Having sold around 730 cars last year, Mini could cross 1,240 units in 2026. Its sales grew 70 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) to 504 units in the first half of the calendar year.
  
Hardeep Singh Brar, president and chief executive officer (CEO) of BMW Group India, told Business Standard that Mini could end the year with growth slightly higher than 70 per cent, aided by the availability of new models in December, traditionally a strong month for luxury car sales.
 
Globally, fully electric cars accounted for 37.2 per cent of Mini’s sales of 2.2 lakh units during January-September 2026, according to BMW Group’s quarterly statement. In India, EVs currently account for around 26 per cent of BMW’s sales.
 
“I think it’s too early because we have just announced the prices today. But I think, to begin with, about 15–20 per cent,” Brar said, when asked about the potential share of EVs in Mini’s India sales.
 
While Mini customers have traditionally preferred petrol-powered cars for their driving characteristics, the company is now seeing a shift towards electric vehicles, he said.
 
Local manufacturing of the petrol-powered Countryman C, launched at ₹47.5 lakh earlier this year, has helped drive volumes. The company has no immediate plans to localise its electric models.
 
Brar said the anticipated benefits of the India-United Kingdom (UK) free trade agreement (FTA) had already been factored into the pricing of the relevant UK-sourced models, alongside adverse foreign exchange movements and commodity costs.
 
Mini has also expanded its presence from eight cities last year to around 19 cities, leveraging BMW’s existing dealership infrastructure. While there are no immediate plans for further network expansion next year, the company will evaluate demand from smaller markets.
 
India remains a relatively small market for Mini globally. Brar said the brand had until recently operated with a limited product portfolio in the country and expects a wider model range to drive volumes in the coming years.
 
Around 25-30 per cent of Mini’s customers in India are first-time luxury car buyers, while the majority already own luxury vehicles and buy a Mini as an additional car. Purchases are often occasion-driven, ranging from anniversary and graduation gifts to additions to existing luxury car collections, Brar said.
 
The new electric Cooper SE, imported as a completely built-up unit (CBU), comes with a 54.2 kWh battery offering a range of 402 km under the Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP), against the 270 km offered by its predecessor. Deliveries will begin immediately.
 
The Paul Smith editions are available across three models — the petrol-powered Cooper S at ₹55.75 lakh, the electric Cooper SE at ₹56.4 lakh, and the Convertible at ₹61.5 lakh. The special editions feature exclusive exterior colours and interior styling inspired by the British designer.

data.title: Apple's retail footprint in India crosses 75,000 sq ft with Hyderabad entry
data.description:
Apple India has leased nearly 12,000 square feet (sq ft) of retail space at Lake Shore Mall in Hyderabad’s Kukatpally, bringing its retail footprint across seven stores in the country to 77,912 sq ft. The store, scheduled to open on December 10, will mark the American technology giant’s entry into Hyderabad.
 
According to property registration documents accessed by Propstack, a real estate data analytics firm, the technology giant signed a fresh lease for 10 years and nine months, starting April 15, 2026, with an option to renew for an additional five years.
 
Under the lease agreement, the technology giant is leasing space on the lower ground and ground floors of the Hyderabad mall.
  
The deal terms include a monthly rent of ₹18.5 lakh for an area spanning 11,890 sq ft. The rent will be paid quarterly at ₹55.51 lakh, translating to a rate of ₹155.50 per sq ft per month.
 
Apple Kukatpally will join the company’s growing network of stores in India, including Apple BKC and Apple Borivali in Mumbai, Apple Saket and Apple Noida in Delhi-NCR, Apple Hebbal in Bengaluru, and Apple Koregaon Park in Pune.
 
Before the Hyderabad addition, Apple’s latest store opened in February 2026 at Oberoi Sky City Mall in Mumbai’s Borivali, spanning 12,616 sq ft. That store was the company’s sixth in India and second in Mumbai.
 
With the addition of the Hyderabad store, Apple’s retail footprint across these seven malls in India will reach 77,912 sq ft. This includes 7,997 sq ft at Phoenix Mall of Asia in Bengaluru, 20,806 sq ft at Jio World Drive in Mumbai, 8,418 sq ft at Select Citywalk in Delhi, 8,240 sq ft at DLF Mall of India in Noida, and 7,945 sq ft at The Kopa in Pune.
 
The store’s barricade, unveiled ahead of the opening, features a pearl-inspired Apple logo against iridescent tones, drawing on Hyderabad’s identity as the ‘City of Pearls’ and its centuries-old tradition of pearl processing and refining.
 
The city, a leading centre for technology and entrepreneurship, also houses Apple’s research and development and retail customer care teams. Apple has been looking to expand its presence in India, which the company has described as a market with significant growth potential.

data.title: HEG lists independently, plans ₹650 crore graphite electrode expansion
data.description:
HEG Limited, an LNJ Bhilwara Group company, on Friday listed its equity shares independently on the BSE and the National Stock Exchange (NSE), following the demerger of its graphite electrode business, as it plans to invest ₹650 crore to expand manufacturing capacity at its Mandideep facility in Madhya Pradesh.
 
The company will increase its annual graphite electrode manufacturing capacity from 100,000 tonnes to 115,000 tonnes, with production from the expanded facility targeted to begin in the first quarter of calendar year 2028.
 
The board has approved the brownfield expansion, which will build on existing infrastructure at less than half the capital intensity of setting up a greenfield plant, the company said in a statement.
 
 
Under the arrangement, shareholders of HEG Advanced Materials Limited (formerly HEG Limited) whose names appeared on the register as of September 7, 2026, received one fully paid-up equity share of HEG Limited (formerly HEG Graphite Limited), with a face value of ₹2, for every share of the same face value held in the erstwhile company.
 
HEG operates the world's largest single-site ultra-high-power (UHP) graphite electrode manufacturing facility at Mandideep, with an annual capacity of 100,000 tonnes. It exports around 65-70 per cent of its production to more than 35 countries and supplies several leading global steelmakers.
 
"Today HEG Limited begins trading as an independently listed company, but the business our shareholders own is the one they have known for nearly fifty years. The same plant, the same people and the same customer relationships now sit within a company focused entirely on graphite electrodes," said Ravi Jhunjhunwala, chairman, managing director, and chief executive officer of HEG Limited.
 
The company said its manufacturing scale and location provide it with the cost competitiveness to navigate business cycles. It also operates an 18 MW captive hydroelectric plant in Tawa and a 6 MW solar plant in Mandideep, which provide power for its energy-intensive manufacturing process.
 
Graphite electrodes are essential consumables in electric arc furnace (EAF) steelmaking. According to the company, EAF steelmaking generates approximately one-fourth of the carbon emissions associated with the blast furnace route.
 
The global shift towards lower-carbon steelmaking, driven by economics, regulation, and the need to reduce emissions, is expected to support demand for graphite electrodes. More than 100 million tonnes of new EAF steelmaking capacity is scheduled to come on stream outside China by 2030, the company said.
 
However, the company said supply cannot respond as easily to the anticipated demand, adding that no new company outside China has entered the graphite electrode industry since 1976.
 
“The listing gives shareholders a direct stake in one of the world's leading graphite electrode businesses, with its own identity and its own capital priorities,” said Riju Jhunjhunwala, vice-chairman of HEG Limited.

data.title: Amazon workers protest over low wages, short-term contracts in 25 cities
data.description:
Amazon warehouse workers, gig workers and trade union members protested across 25 cities in India on Friday, raising concerns over low wages, precarious employment contracts, workplace safety and lack of social security. The protests, organised under the banner of the Amazon India Workers Union (AIWU), were part of the global Make Amazon Pay campaign.
 
In Delhi, more than 200 Amazon warehouse workers gathered, raising concerns over low wages and the use of short-term contracts, particularly for those employed through third-party agencies, which they said kept them out of benefits such as gratuity. 
 
"Current wages are poverty wages and management manipulates short-term contracts to ensure workers do not qualify for gratuity or other benefits, especially those hired through third-party agencies," said Pawan Sisodiya, general secretary of AIWU. 
 
Workers in Delhi also raised concerns over occupational safety at warehouses and insecure employment, calling for better working conditions.
 
An Amazon spokesperson said the group was promoting “a misleading and false narrative”. “The fact is that we are committed to fair and competitive compensation, regularly benchmark our pay against industry standards, and design our practices to comply with applicable laws in every state where we operate,” they said.
 
The spokesperson added that the company works closely with delivery service partners on its network to support their wellbeing. “Associates at our facilities, including those engaged through staffing partners, are covered by Provident Fund and ESIC (Employees State Insurance Corporation) in accordance with applicable law, along with medical, personal accident and term insurance over and above statutory ESIC requirements.”
 
Protests were held in cities including Mumbai, Bengaluru, Jaipur, Kolkata, Patna, Ahmedabad, Pune, Bhopal and Agra. The organisers said memorandums addressed to the respective chief ministers were submitted in all 25 cities, placing the workers' demands before the respective state governments.
 
In Patna, gig and dark-store workers demanded the constitution of a Gig Workers Welfare Board. In Jaipur, warehouse and delivery workers protested under the banner of the All Rajasthan Warehouse Workers Union, according to a release by AIWU.
 
Dharmendra Kumar, president of AIWU, said that data sovereignty was under attack by Amazon. “Community control over data is very important for democracy and sovereignty. Regulating Amazon and having a fair data policy is in the interest of the nation, people and planet,” he said.
 
Gig workers raised concerns over arbitrary blocking of accounts and penalties imposed through platform algorithms. Vandana Narang, spokesperson for the Gig Workers Association, called for an end to such practices.
 
The demand comes amid wider calls for social security coverage for platform workers, including access to welfare benefits and protection against arbitrary account blocking and algorithm-driven penalties.
 
In Thane, 31 organisations joined a protest against Amazon and data centres. In Kolkata, a rally was organised with Hawkers Joint Action Committee, with workers demanding regulation of Amazon and other ecommerce platforms and the immediate implementation of the Street Vendors Act, AIWU said. 
 
The assembly also saw participation from representatives of traders, distributors, street vendors and gig workers. “Amazon and other ecommerce platforms are not only squeezing workers, but at the same time indulging in unfair trade practices to outcompete small and independent traders,” said R K Gaur, general secretary of the Federation of All India Vyapar Mandal (FAIVM).
 
Devender Agrawal, vice-president of the Federation of All India Distributors Association, alleged that Amazon was using predatory pricing and deep discounts, which is affecting traditional distribution networks.
 
The protests were part of the global Make Amazon Pay campaign, co-convened by UNI Global Union and Progressive International. Demonstrations and strikes were organised in more than 20 countries, including Germany and the United States, AIWU said. The campaign, in its seventh year, has called on Amazon to recognise workers' right to organise and negotiate with trade unions.

data.title: RBI urges banks to expedite MSME lending, reduce reliance on collateral
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has urged banks to expedite credit sanctions to micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and reduce their reliance on collateral, encouraging cash-flow-based lending through digital channels to improve access to finance for the sector.
 
At the 31st meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) on MSME credit in Kolkata, Deputy Governor Swaminathan J called for greater use of the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) and other digital channels to facilitate lending to MSMEs, the RBI said in a press release.
 
He also emphasised the need to expand the use of the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) for receivables financing and strengthen early identification and resolution of stress among MSME borrowers.
 
 
The meeting reviewed the flow of working capital and investment credit to MSMEs, lending to first-time borrowers, and credit guarantee coverage. Discussions also covered the enhanced limit for collateral-free lending to micro and small enterprises, settlement of invoices of central public sector enterprises (CPSEs) through TReDS, and key provisions of the MSMED (Amendment) Act, 2026.
 
Recognising the contribution of MSMEs to India's economic growth and development goals, the deputy governor also called on industry associations to actively participate in the RBI's outreach initiatives, including town halls and district-level MSME SAMVAAD meetings.
 
Such engagements would help improve awareness of credit-related initiatives and enable industry associations to raise concerns of their members with banks, according to the RBI.
 
The meeting was attended by representatives of the Ministry of MSME, the Department of Financial Services, select banks, Sidbi, Nabard, CGTMSE, NCGTC, KVIC, the Indian Banks' Association, and national, regional, and state-level MSME associations.

data.title: 136 vessels of Indian interest impacted in troubled waters since March
data.description:
Wars and piracy in global waters have affected 136 vessels of Indian interests in the past eight months, leading to the deaths of 16 Indian seafarers while five remain missing and 34 have been injured, a Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA) report has said.
 
The DGMA’s latest security report covers attacks and other incidents on three major routes between March 1 and November 1. The routes are the Strait of Hormuz/Persian Gulf/Gulf of Oman, the Red Sea/Gulf of Aden/Bab-el-Mandeb, and the Black Sea.
 
The Strait of Hormuz/Persian Gulf/Gulf of Oman region accounted for 93 affected vessels, including six Indian-flagged and 87 foreign-flagged vessels, with 11 fatalities, three missing crew members, and 27 injuries reported.
 
 
In the Red Sea/Gulf of Aden/Bab-el-Mandeb region, six vessels were affected while the Black Sea recorded incidents involving 37 foreign-flagged vessels, resulting in five fatalities, two missing crew members, and six injuries.
 
Overall, the data highlights the significant impact of geopolitical tensions and maritime security threats on commercial shipping and the safety of Indian and foreign seafarers, the DGMA said.
 
11 seafarers still under captivity
The DGMA report also shows that 11 Indian seafarers who were aboard a vessel captured by pirates are still held captive along with 11 foreign seafarers. These seafarers were aboard the MT Asana, which was captured on July 17.
 
The data shows that 46 Indian seafarers have so far been impacted by piracy in the last eight months.
 
Seven incidents related to piracy, hijacking and armed robbery involving vessels with Indian crew members are reflected in the data, the DGMA said.
 
The remaining vessels, except the MT Asana, have been released, have resumed their voyages, or have reported the safe release of their crew, the maritime regulator’s report said.
 
Attacks in war-stricken waters have become a major concern for the government and maritime stakeholders, and seafarer unions have called for a stop to the targeting of commercial vessels.

data.title: Credai seeks affordable housing reforms, tax relief ahead of FY28 Budget
data.description:
The Confederation of Real Estate Developers’ Associations of India (Credai), an industry body representing private real estate developers, has sought reforms to align the definition of affordable housing with current market conditions and improve affordability for homebuyers, among its several suggestions to the finance ministry ahead of the Union Budget 2027-28.
 
Credai said in a statement on Friday that it had also sought enhanced access to housing finance through tax benefits and a reduction in long-term capital gains tax on land and buildings to support sustained investment in the sector, adding that it had shared these recommendations with the ministry during the pre-Budget consultations with Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on November 20.
 
 
The recommendations come against the backdrop of a continued decline in the supply of affordable housing. The share of homes priced below ₹50 lakh across the top eight cities fell from 54 per cent in 2018 to 21 per cent in 2025, the statement showed. This decline reflects the growing affordability challenge amid rising land and construction costs, it added.
 
Separately, data from real estate consultancy Anarock showed that the share of housing supply priced below ₹40 lakh declined from 26 per cent to 10 per cent during the first nine months of 2026.
 
Credai President Shekar Patel said the body's demands for reforms in affordable housing came amid India's expanding housing requirements due to urbanisation and continued strong demand for affordable housing.
 
“There is a need to revisit the existing affordable housing definition to align it with evolving market realities. Tax thresholds need to reflect current property and construction costs,” Patel added.
 
The body has proposed a uniform, area-based definition of affordable housing across goods and services tax (GST), income tax, and priority sector lending. It has recommended limits based on Rera carpet area of 70 square metres (sq m) in notified metros, 90 sq m in urban centres with a population of 10 lakh and above, and 120 sq m elsewhere.
 
If a price ceiling is required for income tax purposes, Credai has recommended raising it to ₹90 lakh, with an annual escalation of 5 per cent to account for inflation and rising raw material and labour costs, the statement said.
 
To improve project viability, the association has sought the reintroduction of the incentive under the former Section 80-IBA through a new Section 142A. The proposal provides for a 100 per cent deduction on profits from eligible projects approved between April 2027 and March 2032. It also seeks to extend the benefit to companies, firms, and limited liability partnerships (LLPs), with exemptions from minimum alternate tax (MAT) and alternate minimum tax (AMT).
 
For homebuyers, Credai has recommended enhancing the tax deduction on housing loan interest for first-time homebuyers under the proposed affordable housing definition. The association has also proposed extending this benefit under both the old and new income tax regimes to improve affordability and encourage homeownership.
 
Further, to expand access to formal housing finance, Credai has proposed strengthening the credit guarantee mechanism for affordable home loans. This includes revising and increasing the existing loan ceiling of ₹20 lakh in line with prevailing market conditions and property rates, with a uniform 75 per cent guarantee cover. Eligibility should be linked to the value of the house rather than the borrower's income category, it said.
 
Credai has also proposed a 10-year income tax exemption on rental income from eligible affordable homes, subject to specified conditions relating to tenancy and vacancy. The measure is aimed at encouraging investment in formal rental housing and increasing the availability of affordable homes in urban centres.
 
A key recommendation is to reduce long-term capital gains tax on land and buildings held for two years or more to 5 per cent, applicable to all taxpayers, including non-residents. The proposal is intended to lower the tax burden on land transactions and encourage landowners to bring land into the development market, particularly through joint development arrangements.
 
The association has also proposed a uniform 5 per cent tax rate on other long-term capital gains and dividend income, subject to specified holding periods and tax provisions. For businesses, it has sought an optional 22 per cent tax regime for partnership firms and LLPs that forgo exemptions, bringing their tax treatment closer to that available to companies.
 
Credai has also recommended a 15 per cent tax rate for new service-sector units established in special economic zones (SEZs) between April 2027 and March 2031, with the benefit available for 10 years. The proposal is aimed at improving the competitiveness of SEZs in attracting new service-sector investment.
 
“Our recommendations seek to address these constraints through targeted fiscal measures that can improve affordability for buyers, make projects viable and encourage the release of land for development. A more consistent tax framework for housing will also support employment, investment and planned urban growth,” Patel said.

data.title: Niti Aayog weighs measures to reduce import dependence in capital goods
data.description:
Amid the growing practice of countries imposing trade curbs on critical components, Niti Aayog is assessing India’s current import dependence in the capital goods market and finalising policy recommendations on both reducing India’s dependence on imports and raising its share in the global supply chain.
 
According to people familiar with the matter, the recommendations could largely be regulatory and institutional, and officials have sought inputs on possible bottlenecks that can be eased to enable more domestic manufacturing of capital goods.
 
“There are two types of dependence. One, where there is complete dependence on other countries for capital goods, and another where a large majority of the manufacturing happens here but crucial components come from countries like China, which know exactly where each critical component they are exporting stands in the global supply chain, and use export controls as leverage. Niti is looking at both these aspects,” an official said.
 
 
The move comes amid increasing calls from the government to increase self-reliance and manufacturing. At the Ficci annual general meeting, Prime Minister Narendra Modi identified hand tools, power tools, and machinery manufacturing – all capital goods – as areas with significant export potential, particularly in developing countries and the Global South.
 
Niti Aayog is likely to prepare a report as part of its trade assessment exercise. Queries sent to Niti Aayog remained unanswered at the time of publication.
 
The move also assumes significance in the wake of recent curbs announced by China on critical construction equipment such as tunnel boring machines (TBMs), which are required by India for major tunnel infrastructure projects across highways, railways, metro rail, and energy.
 
The Cabinet on Wednesday announced an ₹11,000 crore scheme to support the manufacturing of heavy construction equipment to tackle these issues and build an ecosystem in India for what is an important part of the capital goods segment.
 
While it has sought inputs from stakeholders in the sector, the think tank is learnt to be not too keen on financial sops such as tax breaks and manufacturing assistance subsidy programmes. Niti Aayog would look at ways to encourage research and development (R&D), which remains a key area of concern not just in capital goods but across sectors.
 
The Ministry of Heavy Industries has been running the National Capital Goods Policy for a decade, and the second phase of the programme is under way. Under the ₹1,207 crore Phase II, 29 projects have been sanctioned, including centres of excellence, common engineering facilities, testing and certification centres, and technology accelerators.
 
The FY27 Budget also proposed two hi-tech tool rooms to support local design, testing, and production of high-precision components.
 
In a report last week, the Confederation of Indian Industry and Boston Consulting Group recommended a focus on capital goods in emerging sectors such as semiconductors and data centres. Potential approaches include extending selected incentive benefits (e.g., the Semicon India Programme) to domestic capital goods development and procurement, with phased, product-specific domestic value addition (DVA) thresholds verified through factory audits.
 
“Government could also review duty inversions where, for instance, finished equipment used in electronics manufacturing attracts lower duty than inputs and sub-assemblies needed to make it domestically. Any resulting structural cost disadvantage for domestic manufacturers could be addressed by aligning duties on identified inputs,” the report said.
 
It also recommended incentives for R&D and closing the financing gap between Indian players and their global peers.
 
According to the report, India has an import dependence of 38 per cent or more in seven of the 10 subsectors in capital goods, while three subsectors – plastic processing, machine tools, and textile machinery – have import dependence of between 59 and 67 per cent.
